# Massive 20 GWh sodium-ion battery manufacturing plant announced in China

After last year’s slowdown, investment in China’s sodium-ion battery sector is rebounding in 2025, and one of the biggest projects yet has now entered the development pipeline.

By

Nov 24, 2025





Image: China Southern Power Grid Energy Storage



While many lithium-ion battery manufacturers in China are sold out and struggling to keep pace with demand from the energy storage sector, investment is increasingly flowing not only to the ubiquitous lithium-ion technology but also, and substantially, to its key contender: sodium-ion batteries.

With the pipeline of sodium-ion manufacturing plants relentlessly expanding, Guangde Qingna Technology Co., Ltd. officially signed an agreement on Nov. 20 for its 20 GWh sodium-ion battery production project in the Suining Economic and Technological Development Zone, Sichuan Province.

The project represents a total investment of CNY 6 billion ($835.98 million). Once completed, it is expected to create synergies with existing sodium-ion industrial chain projects in the zone.

The Suining Economic and Technological Development Zone is emerging as a major hub for sodium-ion technology development, on the back of several large-scale industrial projects.

For instance, Wuhan Tian Na Technology is building a sodium-ion anode material industrialization base, backed by CNY 58 billion in investment, with a planned output of 130,000 t/year of hard-carbon negative-electrode material. SVOLT is also constructing an anode material project with a reported annual capacity of 1.3 million tonnes, potentially one of the largest sodium-ion anode facilities in the industry.

Furthermore, Suining Tian Na Energy plans another 20,000 t/year sodium-ion material plant with CNY 5.8 billion in investment, while Hive Energy is pursuing a 130,000 t/year sodium-ion negative-electrode material project, broadly aligned with Tian Na’s development.

Currently, the most notable sodium-ion battery production plant in China is the HiNa Battery facility in Fuyang, Anhui Province, built in cooperation with China Three Gorges Corporation and local authorities. The first 1 GWh phase came online in 2022, with the full plan targeting 5 GWh capacity.

Sodium-ion batteries have emerged as a strong contender to lithium-ion technology, often promoted as a cheaper and more sustainable alternative due to sodium’s abundance and low extraction costs. However, they still face challenges before mass-market adoption, including higher costs compared with rapidly scaling lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries.

China currently leads the sector, both in technology development, driven by lithium-ion battery manufacturing heavyweights such as CATL, BYD, EVE and Huawei, and in deployment, with 100 MW-scale projects and multiple hybrid systems combining sodium-ion and lithium-ion batteries, and even grid-forming inverters.

Industry research projects China’s sodium-ion battery market to grow from 10 GWh in 2025 to 292 GWh by 2034, representing an average annual growth rate of roughly 45%. By 2030, China is expected to account for over 90% of global sodium-ion battery production.

According to the recent data from the China Energy Storage Alliance (CESA), 48 sodium-ion battery energy storage production projects were planned in 2024, with a combined annual capacity of 254.7 GWh and a total investment of CNY 126.77 billion, marking a 32% decrease from 2023’s planned capacity of over 375 GWh.

However, data from January to September 2025 indicate that investment in the sector is recovering. During this period, the CESA database recorded 37 new capacity construction projects, totaling 179.5 GWh, already over 70% of last year’s total, including six projects with planned capacities exceeding 10 GWh.

While Guangde’s 20 GWh plant is significant, it is not the largest announced in China. In early 2024, BYD officially started construction of a 30 GWh/year sodium-ion battery plant in Xuzhou, though updates on its progress have been scarce.

| **Sodium-Ion Batteries Enter the Commercial Era** |
| Date:2025-11-01 15:09:32| Views： |
| Evolution & Leap Forward  October 31, 2025 – HiNa Battery successfully hosted a product mass-production launch event themed "Evolution & Leap: From the Product Era to the Commercial Era." This event officially inaugurated the commercial age of sodium-ion batteries, where HiNa will provide customers with high-performance, low-cost sodium-ion battery products, injecting new momentum into the global new energy industry.  The launch began with a retrospective of HiNa Battery's 15-year development journey:   * First Five Years (2011-2015): Focused on fundamental research of sodium-ion battery materials, developing the cathode and anode material systems with the highest industrial potential. * Second Five Years (2016-2020): Progressed from pilot lines to demonstration lines, taking the lead in completing prototype development and application validation for sodium-ion batteries. * Third Five Years (2021-2025): Constructed the world's first thousand/ten-thousand-ton scale material production lines and GWh-scale cell production lines. Conducted application validation across multiple markets, achieving mass production of sodium-ion battery products and market breakthroughs.   After fifteen years, HiNa Battery has systematically completed the full cycle from technology R&D and prototype validation to industrial implementation, laying a solid foundation for the advent of the commercial era.  Standing at the new starting point of the fourth five-year period, HiNa Battery's General Manager, Li Shujun, announced at the event that four sodium-ion battery product lines have now entered the mass-production and sales phase, marking the official transition of sodium-ion batteries from the product era into the commercial era.  Starter Battery: MP10 With a nominal capacity of 10Ah, it features excellent low-temperature, high-rate discharge performance and a long cycle life. Primarily designed for starting/start-stop batteries, it can achieve a lifespan matching that of the vehicle, enabling truly maintenance-free operation for life.  Energy Storage Battery: HE240 With a nominal capacity of 240Ah, this cell is targeted primarily at large-scale energy storage. It has undergone two years of production validation on the GWh-scale cell production line in Fuyang, Anhui. Its mass production and delivery have ensured the successful operation of several sodium-ion battery energy storage power stations in China.  Energy Storage Battery: NE170 With a nominal capacity of 170Ah, it is mainly used for frequency regulation and distributed energy storage, and has already achieved batch delivery and application. Deploying 20% sodium-ion batteries in a 0.25P power station can increase the station's short-term power absorption capacity by 60%, effectively enhancing grid regulation capabilities and renewable energy integration.  Power Battery: MP200 With a nominal capacity of 200Ah, it introduces a new model of "Less Loading, Faster Charging, More Utility." This approach effectively increases total energy output while reducing overall costs, significantly improving the operational economics of commercial vehicles. Recently, the Golden Dragon XMQ4252 pure-electric tractor truck powered by sodium-ion batteries, co-developed by HiNa Battery and Golden Dragon Heavy-Duty Automobile, has been listed in the MIIT product catalog.  Robust manufacturing capability is the core pillar of the commercial era. Currently, HiNa Battery has established ten-thousand-ton scale cathode/anode material production lines and GWh-scale cell production lines. Through deep partnerships with Mianyang Lithium Source and Yuheng Battery, and by collaborating with upstream and downstream partners, HiNa has built a high-quality supply chain system to ensure product consistency and stable delivery capabilities.  Looking ahead, HiNa Battery will continue to deepen its R&D in sodium-ion battery technology and promote multi-scenario, diversified commercial applications. It is projected that by 2028, demand from specific market segments will drive the sodium-ion battery industry to a scale of hundreds of gigawatt-hours. This will propel the industry into its second major leap—transitioning from the commercial era to the scale era—and establish sodium-ion batteries as a central pillar of the global new energy industry. |

results.page_content:
Farasis Energy

Commercial SIB packs achieve 140–160 Wh/kg

Farasis Energy launched commercial sodium-ion battery packs with energy densities of 140–160 Wh/kg, demonstrating that Na-ion performance was approaching the lower end of LFP territory.  
🇨🇳 China

BYD

150Ah blade-type Na-ion cell piloted — 160 Wh/kg, 6,000+ cycles

BYD manufactured a pilot production of a 150Ah blade-type sodium cell achieving 160 Wh/kg energy density and over 6,000 cycles of life, validated through a 20 MWh sodium-ion "Magic Cube" energy storage system.  
🇨🇳 China

Faraday Institution

£19M committed to UK battery research incl. NEXGENNA Na-ion programme

The Faraday Institution announced £19 million in funding across four battery research projects, including the NEXGENNA sodium-ion programme. NEXGENNA targets exceeding LFP performance in energy density, power, and lifetime while maintaining cost, safety, and sustainability advantages.  
🇬🇧 United Kingdom

BYD

Breaks ground on 30 GWh/year Na-ion factory in Xuzhou ($2.25B)

BYD began construction on a massive 30 GWh/year sodium-ion battery facility in Xuzhou City, representing a $2.25 billion investment and signalling that one of the world's two largest battery makers sees Na-ion as a core production chemistry.  
🇨🇳 China

JAC Group / HiNa Battery

China's first mass-produced Na-ion EV delivered

JAC Group's Yiwei brand delivered China's first mass-produced electric vehicle powered by sodium-ion batteries, using cylindrical cells supplied by HiNa Battery Technology. A pivotal moment for Na-ion in mobility applications.  
🇨🇳 China

Sodion Energy

India's first sodium-ion batteries introduced

Sodion Energy launched India's first Na-ion batteries, targeting EVs and home appliances. This signalled growing geographic diversification beyond China in Na-ion commercialisation.  
🇮🇳 India

Kingshine

Cancels proposed 6 GWh Na-ion facility in Jiangxi

Kingshine cancelled its planned 6 GWh sodium-ion battery facility in Jiangxi Province, an early signal that not all Na-ion scale-up ambitions would materialise amid demand uncertainty and financing challenges.  
🇨🇳 China

Natron Energy

First commercial Na-ion factory opens in Holland, Michigan

Natron Energy opened the first commercial-scale sodium-ion battery manufacturing facility in the US, targeting data centre and telecom backup applications with its Prussian-blue electrode chemistry. Capacity: ~600 MW/year.  
🇺🇸 United States

Datang Group

50 MW / 100 MWh grid-scale Na-ion BESS operational in Hubei

China's Datang Group unveiled the first operational grid-connected sodium-ion battery energy storage system at utility scale in Qianjiang, Hubei Province — demonstrating Na-ion viability for renewable energy balancing.  
🇨🇳 China

Altris / Stora Enso

Partnership on bio-waste hard carbon anode materials

Swedish Na-ion developer Altris partnered with Stora Enso to develop Lignode, a hard carbon anode material derived from lignin (bio-waste). This targets a sustainable European Na-ion supply chain with lower embodied carbon.  
🇸🇪 Sweden

Natron Energy

$1.4B gigafactory announced for North Carolina — 24 GWh/year target

Natron Energy announced plans for a $1.4 billion factory in Rocky Mount, NC — the Kingsboro Megasite — projecting 24 GWh annual production by 2028 and over 1,000 jobs. The most ambitious Western Na-ion investment to date.  
🇺🇸 United States

Faraday Institution

UK needs 6 gigafactories by 2030 — Na-ion identified as strategic priority

The Faraday Institution's updated study predicted UK demand for ~120 GWh/year by 2030. CEO Martin Freer stated that sodium-ion technologies offer the UK "an opportunity to take a market-leading position globally in applications beyond automotive."  
🇬🇧 United Kingdom

CATL

Freevoy hybrid battery: Na-ion + Li-ion integrated for PHEVs/EREVs

CATL launched the Freevoy Super Hybrid Battery, integrating sodium-ion and lithium-ion technologies in one pack. It targets plug-in hybrids and extended-range EVs, delivering 400+ km pure electric range with 4C fast charging and extreme temperature performance.  
🇨🇳 China

Reliance New Energy (Faradion)

Completes 100% acquisition of UK's Faradion — Jamnagar gigafactory planned

Reliance New Energy completed the acquisition of Faradion by purchasing the remaining 8% stake (initial deal: €100M in Dec 2021). A Jamnagar gigafactory integrating electrode coatings with petrochemical feedstocks is planned for 2026 start-up, targeting a 10–12% bill-of-materials cost reduction.  
🇬🇧 → 🇮🇳 UK / India

CATL

Second-generation Na-ion battery completed — up to 200 Wh/kg

CATL announced the completion of its second-generation sodium-ion battery achieving energy densities of up to 200 Wh/kg, firmly entering LFP territory. It can discharge reliably at temperatures as low as −40°C.  
🇨🇳 China

BYD

MC Cube-SIB ESS launched — 2.3 MWh per 20ft container

BYD launched a grid-scale sodium-ion battery energy storage system using its Long Blade Battery with CTS super integrated design. While energy density per container is lower than Li-ion equivalents (2.3 vs ~5 MWh), the cost and safety advantages target stationary applications.  
🇨🇳 China

Northvolt

Europe's largest battery start-up files for bankruptcy

Swedish battery manufacturer Northvolt filed for bankruptcy, reportedly burning through $100M/month while struggling to master large-scale manufacturing. BMW had cancelled a $2B contract in June 2024. A sobering signal for European battery manufacturing ambitions.  
🇸🇪 Sweden

Hithium

∞Cell N162Ah — world's first utility-scale Na-ion cell

Hithium unveiled the ∞Cell N162Ah, using sodium-iron pyrophosphate cathode and hard carbon anode. It achieves 94.2% capacity retention after 4,000 cycles at 25°C with a projected lifespan exceeding 20,000 cycles at 70% state of health. GWh-scale production planned for Q4 2025.  
🇨🇳 China

US Department of Energy / LENS Consortium

$50M over 5 years for Na-ion R&D via Argonne National Laboratory

The US DOE, via the LENS Consortium supervised by Argonne National Laboratory, committed $50 million over five years to advance sodium-ion battery technology. A significant increase in US federal support for the chemistry.  
🇺🇸 United States

Yadea

Na-ion powered electric scooters launched — 1,500+ cycles, fast charging

Yadea introduced electric scooters powered by sodium-ion batteries, targeting the massive micromobility market. The cells offer over 1,500 cycles and fast charging capabilities — an ideal use case for Na-ion's cost and safety profile.  
🇨🇳 China

KPIT / Trentar

3 GWh Na-ion production partnership for Indian EV market

KPIT Technologies and Trentar Energy Solutions partnered to build 3 GWh of sodium-ion battery production capacity in India, targeting the electric two-wheeler market where Na-ion's cost advantages are most compelling.  
🇮🇳 India

Altris AB / Volvo Cars Tech Fund

Investment secured for next-gen Na-ion EV and storage development

Altris AB secured strategic investment from the Volvo Cars Tech Fund to co-develop sodium-ion batteries for next-generation electric vehicles and energy storage. A significant European automotive OEM backing Na-ion technology.  
🇸🇪 Sweden

Natron Energy / Draslovka

Czech Republic Prussian blue cathode facility planned

Natron Energy partnered with Draslovka to scale production of Prussian blue cathode materials at a new facility in Kolín, Czech Republic — an attempt to establish European Na-ion supply chain capability. This preceded Natron's subsequent collapse.  
🇨🇿 Czech Republic

BYD

Confirms Na-ion production lines targeting LFP cost parity

BYD confirmed investments in dedicated sodium-ion production lines with the explicit goal of achieving cost parity with lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) batteries — the current benchmark for cost-optimised energy storage.  
🇨🇳 China

CATL

"Naxtra" brand launched — 175 Wh/kg, 10,000 cycles, mass production Dec 2025

CATL launched the Naxtra brand for sodium-ion batteries. The technology achieves 175 Wh/kg energy density (comparable to LFP), 10,000-cycle life, and operates from −40°C to 70°C with 90% energy retention at −40°C. The first application will power Chery EV models.  
🇨🇳 China

China Southern Power Grid

200 MW hybrid Na-ion + Li-ion station in Yunnan

China Southern Power Grid commissioned a 200 MW hybrid storage station in Yunnan combining sodium-ion and lithium-ion batteries to stabilise output from over 30 wind and solar plants. The largest hybrid Na-ion deployment to date.  
🇨🇳 China

JNCASR (India)

Breakthrough: Na-ion cell charges to 80% in 6 minutes, 3,000+ cycles

Researchers at India's Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research unveiled a sodium-ion battery capable of charging to 80% in just six minutes and enduring over 3,000 charge cycles — a significant fast-charging milestone.  
🇮🇳 India

UK Government / Faraday Institution

£452M Battery Innovation Programme announced in Advanced Manufacturing Plan

The UK's Department for Business and Trade announced a multi-year £452 million investment in the Battery Innovation Programme (formerly the Faraday Battery Challenge) as part of the Advanced Manufacturing Sector Plan. Batteries designated a 'frontier industry' within the UK's Industrial Strategy.  
🇬🇧 United Kingdom

Novonix

Na-ion R&D: estimates $125/kWh today, pathway to $30/kWh by 2045

Novonix presented sodium-ion battery R&D covering NFM, NFPP, and Prussian blue cathodes with hard carbon anodes. They estimated current Na-ion cell costs at $125/kWh, with a modelled pathway to $30/kWh by 2045 — potentially transformative for grid-scale storage economics.  
🇺🇸 United States

Natron Energy

Ceases operations — $1.4B gigafactory plans abandoned

Natron Energy shut down after failing to secure working capital, despite raising $363M+ since 2012. UL certification delays prevented order fulfilment; lithium carbonate's 90% price crash undermined Na-ion's cost advantage. The Michigan factory operated less than six months. The North Carolina gigafactory was never built. Assets liquidated through assignment for benefit of creditors.  
🇺🇸 United States

Faraday Institution

£9M for new battery research projects — Na-ion programme continues

The Faraday Institution committed an additional £9 million to battery research, including continued support for sodium-ion alongside projects on electrode manufacturing and battery formation/ageing. The NEXGENNA programme remains part of the broader portfolio.  
🇬🇧 United Kingdom

LG Chem / Sinopec

Joint venture for Na-ion battery materials development

South Korean giant LG Chem partnered with China's Sinopec to develop materials for sodium-ion batteries — a notable sign that established Li-ion players are hedging into Na-ion, driven by competitive pressure from Chinese manufacturers.  
🇰🇷 / 🇨🇳 Korea / China

Peak Energy / Jupiter Power

Grid-scale Na-ion ESS deployment begins in the US

Peak Energy, partnering with Jupiter Power, began deploying grid-scale sodium-ion energy storage systems in the United States — the first meaningful US Na-ion grid installations following Natron's collapse.  
🇺🇸 United States

CATL

Naxtra mass production ramp — first Na-ion EVs on sale (Chery)

CATL's Naxtra sodium-ion batteries are scheduled to enter full mass production, initially powering Chery electric vehicle models. The world's first mass-produced Na-ion passenger cars from the largest global battery manufacturer.  
🇨🇳 China

Reliance / Faradion

Jamnagar gigafactory start-up — India's first Na-ion manufacturing

Reliance's Jamnagar gigafactory, integrating Faradion's UK-developed IP with Reliance's petrochemical feedstock infrastructure, is scheduled for start-up. The facility targets a 10–12% reduction in bill-of-materials costs over competitors.  
🇮🇳 India

TIAMAT

5 GWh Na-ion factory planned in Amiens, France

French Na-ion developer TIAMAT plans to build a 5 GWh production plant in Amiens, producing sodium-ion batteries for data centres, small appliances, and electric vehicles. One of the most significant European Na-ion manufacturing commitments.  
🇫🇷 France

Policy & R&D

2026 (expected)

HiNa Battery

Na-ion cost parity with LFP expected

HiNa Battery has estimated that by 2026, the energy density and cell costs of its sodium-ion batteries will achieve full parity with lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries — a tipping point for large-scale adoption across grid storage and low-cost mobility.  
🇨🇳 China
